From: Evan Doyle
To: Gabriel Fontes, Lucia Mendes
Subject: CAM Reconciliation Dispute – Action Required

Gabriel, Lucia,

We are revisiting the CAM reconciliation disputes for the tenant in question. This is a priority matter that needs to be resolved before month-end close. Please provide a clear status update, including specific disputed line items and any supporting documentation, by Wednesday at 5 PM.

Once we have that, I will schedule a call with the tenant to finalize. If there are any delays, flag them immediately—this cannot slip past the close.

Evan

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Evan Doyle
Subject: RE: CAM Reconciliation Dispute – Action Required

Evan,

Thanks for the nudge. I’m on this and will have the full status update to you by Wednesday at 5 PM, as requested.

For now, here’s the quick read: the disputed items center on two CAM line categories—the shared utilities allocation and the property management fee percentage. I’m pulling the supporting invoices and the lease exhibits for both, plus the detailed calculation sheets we used for the last reconciliation.

I’ll flag anything that looks like it could push past the close as soon as I see it. No red flags at the moment, but I’ll confirm that in the update.

Let me know if you need a preliminary list of the specific line items before Wednesday—happy to send that over sooner.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes

---

From: Evan Doyle
To: Gabriel Fontes, Lucia Mendes
Subject: RE: CAM Reconciliation Dispute – Action Required

Gabriel, Lucia,

Thanks for the quick response, Gabriel. I appreciate the preliminary read on the disputed categories—shared utilities allocation and property management fee percentage.

Please include in the Wednesday update the exact dollar amounts for each disputed line item, the corresponding lease exhibit references, and the calculation methodology used. I also want to see a comparison of what was billed versus what the tenant is claiming, and your recommendation for resolution on each item.

Lucia, please coordinate with Gabriel on the supporting documentation and ensure all invoices are uploaded to the shared drive by Tuesday end of day so we have time to review before the call.

Once we have the full package, I will set up the tenant call for Thursday or Friday of this week—no later than Friday, given the close. If anything shifts, flag it immediately.

Evan

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Evan Doyle
Subject: RE: CAM Reconciliation Dispute – Action Required

Evan,

Thanks for the detailed requirements. I’ll make sure the Wednesday update covers everything you listed — exact dollar amounts per disputed line item, lease exhibit references, calculation methodology, billed vs. claimed comparison, and my recommendation for resolution on each.

Just so you have it now, the two disputed items break down as follows:

1. Shared utilities allocation — the dispute is on the square-footage ratio we applied to the common-area utility invoices. I’m pulling the lease exhibit that defines the allocation method, plus the underlying utility invoices and the calculation sheet from the last reconciliation.

2. Property management fee percentage — the tenant is arguing the fee should be capped at the base percentage in the lease, not the escalated rate we applied. I’m gathering the lease amendment that addresses the escalation and the billing history for comparison.

I’ll have the full package with dollar figures and supporting documents uploaded to the shared drive by Wednesday morning. Lucia is coordinating on the invoice uploads per your note, and I’ll double-check everything is in place by Tuesday end of day.

If anything looks like it could push past the close, I’ll flag it immediately. No current concerns beyond what we’ve already discussed.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes
